observations: THE BRIEF'S STATEMENT OF THE MECHANISM DID NOT SURVIVE MEASUREMENT, AND THAT IS WORTH MORE THAN THE REPAIR. It said the builder's own `landings` assertion fires against a stale source. It does not: the range `baseline..origin/main` is defined by reachability, not by descent, so the synthesised commits are in it even when the baseline and the tip have parted. The symptom is one branch further on - the reading is DIVERGED, so the test returns before the line the mutation edits. Same conclusion, different reason, and a package that had copied the brief's sentence into its record would have shipped a false one.

THE DEFECT IS INVISIBLE IN THE STATE A READER WOULD MOST LIKELY CHECK IT IN, WHICH IS WHY IT SURVIVED FOUR PACKAGES. The record the builder reads comes from the CLONE's working tree, which is a checkout of the source's HEAD. Run from a checkout standing ON `main`, the record and the ref move together and the fixture is right however stale `main` is. Run from a Work Package WORKTREE - which is how every one of these runners is actually invoked - HEAD is the feature branch, its record names a baseline that is on `origin/main`, and local `main` is wherever the last pull left it. So the defect is absent exactly where someone would go looking for it and present exactly where the runner is used.

A CONSTRUCTED SOURCE NEEDS ITS OWN BRANCH, AND THAT IS NOT COSMETIC. Each constructed source is left standing on `wp118-tree-under-test`. Without it, a source whose HEAD happened to BE `main` would hand the fixture builder the record of whatever commit `main` was pointed at, so the three sources would differ in their RECORDS as well as in their refs - two variables and one measurement. The branch keeps the working tree, and therefore the record, identical across all three.

THE AHEAD SOURCE IS THE HALF OF THE QUESTION THE ISSUE DID NOT ASK, AND IT COSTS FOUR CONTROLS - two per builder once the grid runs both. #360 and the brief are about a source that is BEHIND. A source AHEAD of the baseline - the world after some other package merges - is the other direction the fixture must not care about, and a repair that had accidentally pinned the fixture to `baseline` in a way that broke once main moved past it would show up only there. It is also the one PRE-REPAIR cell whose history differs from every other cell's while still reading LAG_EXPECTED: its range carries a THIRD commit, the source's own later package, which the old start point picked up.

THE HARNESS CARRIED AN EIGHTH RUNNER WITH NO NEW PARAMETER AND NO EFFECT ON ITS GUARD. scripts/wp118_controls.py passes NO keyword argument to any defaulted harness parameter - the only keyword it passes at all is `hole=`, which carries no default and is therefore not in the set `tests/test_harness_parameters.py` reads - so it can neither create nor remove a dissenter. The guard's glob is `wp*_controls.py` and now matches eight files; 401 tests OK is the measurement that it did not mind.

THE ONE COPIED LINE IS WRITTEN AS A MUTATION SO THAT IT CANNOT GO STALE IN SILENCE. The pre-repair builder could have been transcribed into wp118_controls.py as a second function; then a later edit to the real builder would leave the copy measuring a version of the defect nobody has any more. Written as `edit(copy, WP112, REPAIRED, BEFORE_THE_REPAIR)` it asserts the repaired line is still present, so the control fails loudly the day the repair is reworded.

THE FIXTURE'S COMMITS NOW CARRY THE BASELINE'S TREE RATHER THAN THE TIP'S, AND NOTHING READS IT. `commit-tree` is given `{tip}^{tree}` and `tip` starts at the baseline, so the synthesised commits carry the baseline's tree. Nothing is checked out, so the clone's WORKING TREE is still the source's HEAD and still carries the module under test, which is the property the docstring promised and still promises. The reconciliation and its test read subjects and ancestry only.

THE `AT BASELINE` SOURCE IS ALSO WHAT THIS WORKTREE IS, WHICH IS WHY THE SYMPTOM COULD NOT BE FOUND BY RUNNING THE RUNNER PLAINLY. `refs/heads/main` here is 6958e84, the recorded baseline this package rolls to, so a plain `python scripts/wp112_controls.py` from this worktree exercises the AT BASELINE case and passes on both sides of the repair. The reproduction had to be constructed, and the constructed source is the one the before/after diff was taken on.

THE COORDINATOR'S BRIEF AND THE REVIEWER AGREED AGAINST EACH OTHER ON TWO POINTS, AND BOTH WERE SETTLED BY MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN BY AUTHORITY. The brief said the builder's `landings` assertion fires on a stale source; it cannot, and the review upheld that. The first draft of this package said that assertion became a construction check with #360; it had been one since WP-112, and the review caught that. The same instrument settled both - build the fixture the old way on a parted history and read what the assertion would have seen.

DECLARING WHICH CONTROLS DISCRIMINATE WAS ASKED FOR AS PROSE AND IS SHIPPED AS FOUR MORE CONTROLS. The AT BASELINE and AHEAD pairs pass on both sides of the repair, so a reader could reasonably read three pairs as three measurements of one repair when only one of them is. Running the pre-repair builder against all three sources rather than against BEHIND alone adds four controls - eight to twelve - and four suite runs - nine to thirteen - and puts the answer in the output: five of the six cells behave the same way and the sixth does not. The sentence no longer has to be believed.

A DOCSTRING PARSED BY A CONTROL IS BEHAVIOUR, AND THE RULING THAT `A DOCSTRING IS NOT BEHAVIOUR` IS TOO BROAD FOR THIS REPOSITORY. The narrower rule, recorded because this package leaned on the broad one: prose is safe to edit unless something parses it, and the way to know is to LOOK. `scripts/wp114_controls.py`'s fifteenth control parses the very module docstring this package edited - it reads the `grep -lnE` command out of it, compiles the pattern the sentence carries, and compares the modules the sentence NAMES against the modules the tree measures, so a `test_*.py` name added anywhere in that docstring would have broken it. Run against this head: True, `4 modules call one, 9 mention the word: ['test_resume_reconciliation.py', 'test_resume_schema_identity.py', 'test_validator_fails_closed.py', 'test_wp024_fixtures_are_sealed.py']`. Two AST-identity comparisons said the edit changed no code; this says it changed nothing a control reads either.
assumptions: That a fixture built entirely from the record is better than one built from a ref, even though it costs two of the builder's three assertions their ability to report on anything outside the builder. The alternative - keeping a source-dependent start point and asserting harder about it - was rejected because #360 asks for independence, and because an assertion that fires on the ordinary state of a fetched-but-not-pulled checkout is a false failure of the kind check_source_main_line already exists to prevent.

That behind, at and ahead span what matters about a source's main line for this fixture. Nothing here constructs a source with no `main` ref at all, a shallow source, or a source whose record names a baseline it does not hold. The last of those is what the builder's new assertion answers and it is declared as uncovered below rather than measured.

That correcting the WHAT IT DOES NOT PROMISE paragraph is inside this package's scope. It is in the file this package edits, its claim is measurably false, and this package's own change is what removes the last reading under which it could have been true - leaving it beside a repair of the thing it described seemed worse than the widening. #357's precedent, that a package does not widen its diff into a sibling's prose, points the other way, and a reviewer may rule that it should have been filed instead.

All six siblings were enumerated for the defect class - a fixture built from a ref rather than from the record: wp114's two builders start from `recorded_baseline(root)` and were already independent of the source, and wp111, wp113, wp115, wp116 and wp117 synthesise no history at all. WP-114 IS ALSO THE ONE SIBLING THIS PACKAGE COULD HAVE BROKEN, and the first draft of this entry left it out of the list: its fifteenth control parses the module docstring this package edits. Measured against this head - True, 4 modules call a subprocess, 9 mention the word. Nothing else about any sibling was checked.

THE CORRECTED DOCSTRING PARAGRAPH IN scripts/wp112_controls.py IS PROSE AND NO TEST HOLDS IT. It no longer restates a count of that runner's own controls - a count written into the file it counts goes stale the day someone adds one - and points at scripts/wp118_controls.py as the standing evidence instead. What it still asserts is a relation: that a behind `main` costs the ordinary controls nothing. Only someone running the runner again would catch that going stale.

THE `AHEAD` SOURCE'S SYNTHESISED COMMIT IS NOT A MERGE AND CARRIES THE BASELINE'S TREE. Real main-line commits in this repository are squash merges of a branch with a different tree; nothing in the reconciliation or its test reads a tree, so the difference is declared rather than removed.

THE GRID IS THREE SOURCES BY TWO BUILDERS AND NOTHING WIDER. It does not vary the record, the mutation, or the test module; the pre-repair builder differs from the repaired one by exactly one line, so the grid measures that line and nothing else about either builder.

FOUR OF THE SIX REPAIRED CONTROLS ARE INVARIANCE INSURANCE, NOT EVIDENCE, and six controls should not be read as six measurements. After the repair the builder reads no ref, so the three REPAIRED cells build ONE IDENTICAL HISTORY: `git log --format='%T|%s'` over `baseline..origin/main` prints the same tree and the same two subjects in all three. The AT BASELINE and AHEAD pairs therefore assert a property rather than measure the repair, at four clones and four suite runs. They are kept because that property is what #360 bought and is worth asserting once the builder stops reading refs. The PRE-REPAIR row is not in this declaration: its three histories genuinely differ - AT BASELINE identical to the repaired one, AHEAD carrying a third commit and still LAG_EXPECTED, BEHIND parted and DIVERGED - so all six of its controls carry information.
